title: Topological learning and simulations predict lithium superionic-conductor candidates
summary: A multiscale topological-learning workflow combined algebraic-topology descriptors, unsupervised clustering and ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations to screen lithium-containing structures. The study reports 14 candidate conductors meeting computational thresholds for diffusion barriers and electrochemical stability. The reported conductivities are simulated, with ambient values estimated from elevated-temperature trajectories. Some candidates had prior experimental reports or patents cited by the authors; those are not experimental validation produced by this AI workflow. Many candidates remain untested.
ai_technology: Multiscale topological learning; persistent homology; affinity propagation clustering; ab initio molecular dynamics

source_review.scope: Primary PMC full text and publication metadata; article identity, methods, bounded computational outcomes and affiliation block.

evidence.tested: The study used ab initio molecular-dynamics simulations to estimate conductivity, diffusion barriers and electrochemical stability for 45 selected candidate materials and reports 14 meeting its computational thresholds.
evidence.unknown: Conductivities are computational estimates, including Arrhenius extrapolation from elevated-temperature simulations; source-cited experimental reports for some materials predate or are independent of this AI workflow, and other candidates remain untested.
evidence.ai_role: Topological feature extraction and unsupervised learning screened structures and prioritized candidate clusters; AIMD simulations evaluated specific candidate transport claims.
